perspective: Adversarial verification of change requests, amendments, termination, permissions, and audit history against all three interview transcripts and derived Markdown artifacts.

findings.claim: Late changes can include job code, hours, and hourly rate changes after the original appointment is complete.

evidence.quote: change ... one's going to be 10 hours TA, 10 hours RA and the other one's switching to 20 hours RA
I need to issue a new offer letter ... change ... hourly rate, increase it ... initiate it
asking for like a change in their job code ... only certain users would need to have the feature to overwrite

findings.risk: A single mutable appointment row can erase the original terms and obscure which fields changed.
findings.recommendation: Represent each amendment as a distinct request/event with old value, new value, requester, timestamp, rationale, and affected assignment; do not overwrite history.

findings.claim: The operational submitter for student changes is Mayra, while HR/Finance execute their respective downstream work; faculty may still send requests directly, creating an intake exception.

evidence.quote: 10% sent it to me and Daisy and Jamie ... if this was done in the apps, Mayra got this change request
all the students go through Mayra ... she should be submitting the request to me ... If it's there, I do it
faculty ... asking for like a change in their job code ... restrict that to particular people

findings.risk: Derived artifacts can incorrectly model faculty as the formal change-request owner while the interview says Mayra is the intended intake owner.
findings.recommendation: Separate requester (faculty/supervisor), submitter/intake owner (Mayra for student requests), executor (Laura or Finance), and approver if any. Preserve direct-email exceptions as intake evidence, not as the normal authorization path.

findings.claim: An amendment repeats the offer-letter and Oracle amendment work; re-running foreign-principal screening is not established.

evidence.quote: I need to issue a new offer letter ... amend them because they've already been [appointed]
RA to TA ... foreign principle, letter, enter, make the change actually
Change request ... Laura issues a new letter, may redo the screening, amends Oracle

findings.risk: The derived phrase 'may redo the screening' is not supported by the transcript and could cause unnecessary or incorrect screening behavior.
findings.recommendation: Treat new offer-letter issuance and Oracle amendment as confirmed for relevant changes. Mark screening repeat as unresolved unless an owner specifies field/change conditions that require it; do not implement it from the summary alone.

findings.claim: Funding/chartfield changes are visible to Finance and trigger costing rework, but the exact approval gate is not a generic request-approval step.

evidence.quote: changes to the funding ... Daisy and Jamie can see funding, the new funding, to then obviously do the costing
If we need to change the chart field, we'll go in here and change it ... once it's entered, I change it ... put the date and the initials
Finance verifies the chartfield ... No money ... update the worksheet, re-verify ... Enter costing in Oracle
not for approvals ... there's not really an approval as such

findings.risk: A generic approval workflow would misrepresent the stated process; funding changes may require verification, new account resolution, and costing rather than an app approval.
findings.recommendation: Model Finance verification/re-verification and costing as explicit work states. Do not infer a separate approval gate from the change-request concept.

findings.claim: Termination requests are expected to be recorded in the app, normally submitted through Mayra for student appointments; Finance may terminate an ended appointment in its worksheet after confirmation.

evidence.quote: Mayra had asked me to appoint ... we ended it ... having something in one place ... Mayra would go in and just say ... terminate this person
Mayra could have went in and said, please terminate this employee ... all the student requests should be going through Mayra
anybody that's left, I terminate them here and it removes them from this summary
Ended -> terminate in the worksheet

findings.risk: If termination is modeled as an unrestricted edit, an executor can remove an active appointment without preserving the request, reason, effective date, or confirmation.
findings.recommendation: Use a termination-request record with requester, confirmer/authority, reason, effective date, and execution status. Keep the active appointment history; mark it ended rather than deleting it. Enforce Mayra intake for student requests and Finance execution only for the finance active-summary/worksheet behavior unless policy is clarified.

findings.claim: Permissions are field/workflow-specific, not simply global read/write; users need broad visibility but only designated users may edit certain stages.

evidence.quote: Mayra ... edit ... requested changes ... sent over to you
gate changes behind certain people ... everybody view access ... permissions ... each role
those statuses only applied to her ... only certain people have access to edit certain screens ... no reason for me to ... change any of her statuses
sensitive information ... Finance team has access ... only some people should be able to edit particular things

findings.risk: A broad 'anybody can see anything' implementation could expose sensitive finance data, while unrestricted edits could bypass HR/Finance ownership.
findings.recommendation: Define permissions by actor, entity/field, action, and lifecycle state. Treat Ian's proposed broad visibility as design proposal, not confirmed policy; explicitly resolve Finance data visibility and amendment execution rights.

findings.claim: Audit/history is a mandatory requirement: preserve original requests and amendment/termination actions rather than overwriting the row.

evidence.quote: they just overwrite the spreadsheet ... no trail as a request ... concern ... duplicating
notes text box for each action ... tracking what's done
find evidence for the auditors ... history of the request ... all in the one place
log system or ... History of changes and note-taking
status ... date and the initials

findings.risk: Without immutable history, audit reconstruction depends on email/Teams searches and cannot prove who requested, changed, verified, or terminated an appointment.
findings.recommendation: Require append-only audit events for create, submit, edit/amend, status transition, verification, costing, termination, and permission-sensitive actions. Capture actor identity, timestamp, field-level before/after values, source/request text, and linked assignment/request IDs.

findings.claim: The derived pipeline's D4 loop and entry-point model are too strong: they encode a faculty-owned change request and return directly to Mayra's log step, while the transcripts establish multiple intake routes and do not settle exact routing for every amendment.

evidence.quote: Change request ... owner faculty ... change_request -> log_request
request ... sent to me and Daisy and Jamie ... if ... apps, Mayra got this change request
all the student requests should be going through Mayra
Does a late change go back to Mayra, or only to Laura ... open questions

findings.risk: A hard-coded loop can route amendments to the wrong owner or imply that direct faculty requests are authorized edits.
findings.recommendation: Replace the single D4 loop with an explicit intake/request entity and routing rules per change type. Keep the route unresolved until owners define whether job-code/hour/rate/funding/termination requests each follow the same path.

missing_or_ambiguous: Whether foreign-principal screening repeats for any amendment, and which field changes trigger it.
Whether hiring-authority signature is required again for each amendment, versus only a new student offer or selected changes.
Whether student termination requires Laura/HR approval, faculty confirmation, Finance confirmation, or only Mayra submission plus Laura execution.
Whether Finance may directly edit chartfields in the canonical appointment record or must submit a change to another owner.
The exact permission matrix for Mayra, Laura/HR colleague, hiring authorities, Daisy/Finance, faculty, and students.

Whether audit history must be immutable/append-only and whether amendment snapshots must include field-level before/after values; the need for history is confirmed but the technical retention policy is not.
The exact status/state machine for requested, approved/accepted, in-progress, executed, rejected, superseded, and terminated amendments.
Whether a late change creates a new assignment/version or mutates the existing assignment's effective-dated record.
